problem:
Which of the following vector spaces has a dimension of $15?$

- ${\text{M}}_{3\times 5}(R),$ the vector space of all $3\times 5$ matrices over $R$
- ${R}_{15}[t]$, the vector space of all polynomials in the variable $t$ of degree at most $15$
- ${R}^{15}$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying True Statements About Dimensions of Vector Spaces
examples.problem:
Which of the following vector spaces has a dimension of $9?$

- $\mathbb{R}^8$

- $\mathbb{R}_8[t]$, the vector space of all polynomials in the variable $t$ of degree at most $8$

- $\text{M}_{3}(\mathbb{R}),$ the vector space of all $3 \times 3$ matrices over $\mathbb{R}$
examples.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the vector spaces in turn.

- Recall that $\textrm{dim}(\mathbb{R}^n)=n.$ Therefore, 

$$
\textrm{dim}(\mathbb{R}^8)=8\neq 9.\quad {\color{red}{\times}}
$$

- Recall that $\textrm{dim}(\mathbb{R}_{n}[t])=n+1.$ Therefore, 

$$
\textrm{dim}(\mathbb{R}_{8}[t])=8+1=9.\quad {\color{green}{\checkmark}}
$$

- Recall that $\textrm{dim}(\text{M}_{n}(\mathbb{R}))=n^2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\text{dim}(\text{M}_{3}(\mathbb{R}))=3^2=9.\quad {\color{green}{\checkmark}}
$$

Hence, the correct answer is "II and III only."

feedback.problem: What is the dimension of ${\text{M}}_{10\times 2}(R),$ the vector space of all $10\times 2$ matrices over $R?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard basis of ${\text{M}}_{n\times m}(R)$ contains a total of $n\cdot m$ matrices, each with one nonzero entry that is equal to $1.$ 

For example, the standard basis of ${\text{M}}_{3\times 2}(R)$ contains $3\cdot 2=6$ elements, and is given by

$$
{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Therefore, for ${\text{M}}_{10\times 2}(R),$ we have

$$
\text{dim}({\text{M}}_{10\times 2}(R))=10\cdot 2=20.
$$

In general, 

$$
\text{dim}({\text{M}}_{n\times m}(R))=n\cdot m.
$$
